title: Converge minimal runtime images, lockfile hygiene, and remote cache warmup
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our CI build matrix has accumulated multiple, slightly different Node/Python base images, ad-hoc apt packages installed during image builds, and an inconsistent approach to lockfiles. This increases image churn, reduces remote cache hit rates, and causes unpredictable PR build times. Recent incidents (pipeline timeouts on 2026-01-06 and 2026-01-20) traced to cold cache and multiple identical dependency install phases across jobs.

Goal: Reduce PR build latency and variability by consolidating to a small set of reproducible runtime images, enforcing lockfile hygiene, and implementing a deterministic remote cache warmup path for common PRs. This ticket covers the engineering work for the image consolidation, package manager alignment, and an automated cache-priming job that runs pre-merge for high-volume repos.

Why this matters: Lower median PR feedback time (~30% target), fewer flakes due to environment drift, and better cache utilization leading to lower CI bill. This also makes future security upgrades (OS and package upgrades) simpler because there are fewer images to patch.
acceptance_criteria: Median PR build time for core repos reduced by at least 30% over the 30-day baseline (measured on ci.redwood.internal/dashboard)
Remote build cache hit rate for docker layer and buildkit cache >= 80% for normal PR runs
All active build pipelines use one of the approved minimal base images (redwood/base-node:16-slim-min, redwood/base-py:3.11-slim-min) and documented derivation
Lockfile enforcement implemented: npm/pnpm/yarn (whichever repo uses) and pip-tools lock step run in CI that fails fast on missing or out-of-sync lockfiles
Automated cache warmup job added to nightly pipeline that pre-populates frequently used layers; measured cold cache failures reduced by 90% on rollout
A migration doc + rollback plan exists and is linked; at least two repos successfully migrated in pilot with no regressions for 2 weeks
plan: Audit: enumerate current base images and packages used across top-20 active repos (day 1-3)
Design: decide on canonical minimal images (Node / Python / Go) and publish Dockerfiles + SBOMs (day 4-7)
Prototype: build new images with buildkit, layer squashing and reduced apt installs; integrate remote cache (day 8-14)
Lockfiles: add CI checks to validate lockfile freshness and introduce a pre-commit hook template (day 10-16)
Cache warmup: add a dedicated job that runs against the remote cache to prime common layers and dependency installs (day 12-18)
Pilot migration: migrate 2 medium-sized repos (sdk-js, infra-ci) and monitor metrics/roll back if regressions (day 18-28)
Rollout: incrementally migrate remaining repos and deprecate legacy images (day 29-45)
Post-mortem & docs: publish migration runbook, image maintenance cadence, and cost/latency results (day 46+)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Some repos depend on OS packages or native binaries not present in minimal image. Mitigation: provide a small apt-extension pattern and per-repo overlay image template; run a compatibility scanner during audit.
Risk: Lockfile update churn for large repos. Mitigation: provide an automated bot PR that updates lockfiles on a schedule and include a migration window for human review.
Risk: Cache warmup job may increase CI cost if misconfigured. Mitigation: cap warmup concurrency, only target high-value layers, and monitor warmup cost vs. savings weekly.

Risk: Rollout causes flaky builds due to subtle environment differences. Mitigation: pilot on two repos, preserve ability to select previous base with a per-pipeline override for 2 weeks after migration.
progress_updates: 2026-01-11: Kickoff audit completed for 24 repos; identified 3 major OS package families and 7 repos with native build deps (build-logs linked).
2026-01-18: Prototype minimal node and python images built with buildkit + reproducible layer ordering; initial size reductions: node image -38%, python image -31%.
2026-01-25: Implemented lockfile check step in the pipeline (experimental) and configured to run as a non-blocking warning for 1 week to surface breakage.
2026-02-05: Cache warmup job drafted and ran in staging for 48 hours; remote cache hit rate improved from 22% to 74% for targeted jobs during warmup window.
2026-02-12: Began pilot migration of sdk-js repo; first run failed due to missing libpq-dev — added overlay template and re-ran successfully.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-01-12): Audit results pushed to Confluence. Noted two repos still on Node 14 — we should schedule small bump PRs before migration.
Arjun Patel (2026-01-19): Prototype builds look good; will add test runner image variants for mutating integration tests next week.
SRE team (2026-01-20): Please ensure warmup job respects rate limits toward our remote cache backend — we hit a rate limit in staging earlier today.
Design (2026-01-22): Request that image SBOMs expose origin of each apt package to help security team triage CVEs.
Arjun Patel (2026-02-06): Cache warmup results promising; plan to schedule weekly warmups and gate additional scalars behind cost guardrails.
